No security-critical input parsing bugs found; PEM/DER framing is delegated to x509-cert which is the right call. The P0 is the single must-fix before 1.0; the P1s are 'decide now while pre-1.0 breaking changes are cheap.'
Confidence: ~10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-tit4.5 (IoFailure location is forward-looking, depends on whether sibling adapter crates actually grow io-error needs). API contract risk: MEDIUM — one P2 doc/impl mismatch (PKIX-tit4.11: from_der_iter docs say 'all anchors decoded' but impl is fail-fast), one P3 factually-wrong doc (PKIX-tit4.12: MalformedAnchor doc references from_pem but only from_der_iter produces it), three P3 underspecified semantics callers will hit (iteration order, dedup, panic safety), one P3 docs gap on Send+Sync, plus two opinion-flagged structural concerns (no Loader struct, no partial-load API). No P0/P1 contract findings beyond what was already filed in the main pass. The contract is broadly sound — Error is #[non_exhaustive], DerError/IoFailure correctly insulate from upstream version churn, free-function shape is idiomatic — but has rough edges around fail-fast semantics and several caller-visible behaviors that exist in code but not in rustdoc.

- B (Side-channel hygiene): N/A. No equality comparisons on secret bytes. The single byte-equality compare in the crate is `*w == b"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"` at lib.rs:325-326 (and the equivalent in tests/fixtures.rs:78), which compares input bytes against a public constant — no secret participates. No table lookups by secret index, no early-return on padding-byte mismatch.

- C (Untrusted input at protocol boundaries): IN SCOPE; no new findings. Six entry points re-audited: from_pem (lib.rs:314), from_der (349), from_der_iter (371), from_pem_file (397), from_der_file (410), io_error_kind_serde::deserialize (170). All parsing delegates to total parsers in x509-cert / der (Certificate::from_der calls Decode::from_der which calls reader.finish() rejecting trailing bytes; verified prior pass at ~/WORK/formats/der/src/decode.rs:84-89). The BEGIN_BOUNDARY window guard at lib.rs:324-329 correctly defends against the upstream subtract-with-overflow panic mode in x509-cert 0.2.x's load_pem_chain (fixed upstream per #1965; workaround documented inline). Negative-test coverage exhaustively pins typed-error behavior: from_der_garbage_errors, from_der_iter_reports_index_of_malformed_entry, truncated_pem_block_errors, garbage_after_begin_boundary_errors, unknown_pem_label_errors, from_der_file_missing_path_errors. No reachable panic. The only real DoS vector — unbounded fs::read for from_pem_file/from_der_file — is already filed as PKIX-tit4.24 at P2. The io_error_kind_serde::deserialize unknown-kind→Other fallback is non-destructive forward-compat insurance; the deserialized kind string is used only as a dispatch key, never executed or echoed.

- D (Random source quality): N/A. No RNG consumed anywhere in the crate. `rg -n "OsRng|thread_rng|rand::|getrandom" pkix-truststore/` returns zero matches.

- E (Persistent storage of secrets): N/A. No secrets persisted. The crate reads cert bytes from the filesystem (public data) and emits TrustAnchor values; no secret leaves volatile memory because no secret enters it.

- F (Logging output safety): N/A. `rg -n "info!|warn!|error!|debug!|trace!|println!|eprintln!|tracing::|slog::|log::" pkix-truststore/` returns zero matches. Error::Display content (lib.rs:239-249) renders cert/PEM/Der/IoFailure messages — all public data. No blacklist exposure surface exists.

- G (Algorithm and parameter choice): N/A. No cryptographic primitives invoked. The crate parses certificates structurally; signature verification, hash computation, and trust-anchor self-signature checks are deliberately out of scope.
